channel.title: AI Agents in Practice

item.title: David Heinemeier Hansson (DHH) — The a16z Show (Martin Casado & Anish Acharya): Why AI Has DHH Working 16-Hour Days (Why the Agent Era Needs a New Operating System)
item.description:
David Heinemeier Hansson (DHH) (37signals) — The a16z Show (Martin Casado & Anish Acharya): Why AI Has DHH Working 16-Hour Days (Why the Agent Era Needs a New Operating System)

  • New: Declares 'anyone who still thinks there is moat in source code are delusional' and positions Omarchy as an agent-first OS that users reshape by prompting.
  • New: Explains why Linux's terminal, plain config files and detailed errors are 'the three things agents love,' calling macOS at risk of becoming 'the AOL of the agent era.'
  • New: Admits working 16-hour days (despite co-authoring It Doesn't Have to Be Crazy at Work) because agents collapsed the barrier between spotting a 2-pixel flaw and fixing it.
  • New: Cites an Omarchy community member rebuilding an Adobe Lightroom replacement in two weeks, and reports ~$23M to $24M in pledges and tokens for the Omacom Foundation (founder-reported).

Stories: Agents write 100% of Omarchy Quattro, an agent-native Linux desktop

item.title: Simon Willison — AI Engineer CODE Summit 2026: 2026 in LLMs
item.description:
Simon Willison (Independent) — AI Engineer CODE Summit 2026: 2026 in LLMs

  • New: Organizes 2026 into three inflection points—Nov 2025 daily coding agents (Opus 4.5 / GPT-5.1), persistent goal-pursuing 'Fable-class' models, and iterative agent-built games that become genuinely fun.
  • New: Tells the Beep Locator story—Claude turned five household devices into a microphone array using a 2007 paper (BeepBeep) to find a beeping CO detector in 40 moving boxes to within 41 cm.
  • New: Shares a 12-hour Opus 5.5 loop that ran ~1,000 simulated battles to turn a real-time strategy prototype into a game he genuinely enjoyed.
  • New: Quotes Greg LeMond ('It doesn't get easier, you just get faster')—delegating easy work leaves humans with harder decisions and more plates spinning.

Stories: Claude turns five household devices into a microphone array to find a mystery beep · Opus 5.5 runs 1,000 simulated battles overnight to make a game genuinely fun

Watch on YouTube ↗ · Full profile

item.title: Armin Ronacher — AI Engineer CODE 2026: The Software Atelier (Build the Workshop Before the Software Factory)
item.description:
Armin Ronacher (Earendil) — AI Engineer CODE 2026: The Software Atelier (Build the Workshop Before the Software Factory)

  • New: Shows charts from his own Pi sessions—with no change to Pi's core tools, corrections fell with every model and P90 task runtime rose from ~2.5 minutes in Dec 2025 to 14+ minutes by Nov 2026.
  • New: Compares 141 Git repositories he started over the year against only ~10 to 15 kept active past five days, arguing human attention—not code generation—is the real ceiling.
  • New: Has agents generate short typeset HTML executive summaries around 70% through a run so he can inspect tradeoffs even when not reading every line of code.
  • New: Makes the case for combining 'code mode' (agents writing small orchestration scripts) with fast classifier models to triage thousands of incoming requests cheaply, alongside durable suspend-and-resume runtimes.

Stories: Same four-tool harness jumps from 2.5-minute to 14-minute task runs · 141 agent-started repos reveal that human attention is the ceiling · Earendil ships Pi 1.0 and Pi Durable for crash-safe agents

Watch talk & transcript ↗ · Full profile

item.title: Tobi Lütke — Sources with Alex Heath: Shopify CEO on why using AI isn't optional
item.description:
Tobi Lütke (Shopify) — Sources with Alex Heath: Shopify CEO on why using AI isn't optional

  • New: Says quiet AI skeptics will not become top performers next to colleagues using agents, and companies should say this openly.
  • New: Criticizes open-source projects that ban AI contributions. Good code should be accepted whoever or whatever wrote it.

item.title: Guillermo Rauch — Sourcery with Molly O'Shea: 60% of Vercel Deployments Are Now Shipped by AI Agents
item.description:
Guillermo Rauch (Vercel) — Sourcery with Molly O'Shea: 60% of Vercel Deployments Are Now Shipped by AI Agents

  • New: Puts the agent share of deployments at 60%, up from 'more than half' in June, and says Vercel added 1.5 billion deployments in 10 months.
  • New: Says open models now carry about 80% of tokens on Vercel's network, with frontier models planning and cheaper open models doing routine work.
  • New: Vercel ran a $1 million sandbox challenge, and one researcher working with many agents found a serious issue. He says most companies have not solved agent security.
  • New: Says an agent did the first pass of the Mercedes F1 team's site migration in five minutes.

Stories: Coding agents now trigger most Vercel deployments · Agent does first pass of an F1 team's site migration in five minutes

item.title: Armin Ronacher — Pi Durable Deep Dive (with Mario Zechner): Pi Durable: Agents That Survive Crashes — Mario Zechner & Armin Ronacher
item.description:
Armin Ronacher (Earendil) — Pi Durable Deep Dive (with Mario Zechner): Pi Durable: Agents That Survive Crashes — Mario Zechner & Armin Ronacher

  • New: Walks through the architecture of Pi Durable (shipped Oct 1 alongside Pi 1.0), where every model turn and tool call checkpoints to storage so a crashed agent resumes where it left off.
  • New: Explains why tool replay boundaries are the hardest part of durable agents—deciding what can safely re-run versus what had external side effects.
  • New: Discusses pairing coding agents with fast single-shot classifier models for high-volume routing and triage rather than sending every branch through a slow frontier LLM.

Stories: Earendil ships Pi 1.0 and Pi Durable for crash-safe agents

item.title: Geoff Charles — Lenny's Podcast (Lenny and Friends Summit talk): What product looks like when coding is solved | Geoff Charles (Ramp CPO)
item.description:
Geoff Charles (Ramp) — Lenny's Podcast (Lenny and Friends Summit talk): What product looks like when coding is solved | Geoff Charles (Ramp CPO)

  • Changed view: with coding largely solved, the bottleneck has moved to product work, so PMs should build the factory: agents to identify, define, build, coordinate and improve.
  • New: Inspect builds 75% of PRs (up from about 50% in March); Review Buddy handles 93% of PRs; Testo caught 425 bugs in 30 days.
  • New: 60% of flagged UX issues fixed within 24 hours, and an agent answers 85% of questions sent to PMs. Repeats the customer feedback agent from March, now at larger scale.
  • New: splits PM work into three tracks (factory builders, tastemakers, GMs) and said "Everything you've seen here is outdated." Numbers come from third-party write-ups, not a transcript.

Stories: Customer feedback agent does 8 days of analysis in minutes · Inspect coding agent builds 75% of Ramp's pull requests · Review and QA agents handle 93% of PRs and caught 425 bugs in 30 days · 60% of reported UX issues fixed within 24 hours

item.title: David Heinemeier Hansson (DHH) — Rails World 2026 (Austin): Rails World 2026 Opening Keynote - DHH
item.description:
David Heinemeier Hansson (DHH) (37signals) — Rails World 2026 (Austin): Rails World 2026 Opening Keynote - DHH

  • Changed view: Declares 37signals has gone 'pencils down' on handwritten code as the default and says he has retired from professional hand-coding, tracing his tipping point to Claude Opus 4.5 (Nov 24, 2025).
  • New: Shares the Basecamp 5 lesson—designers opened 20 to 30 individually reasonable agent PRs that together left the architecture in poor shape, requiring substantial human cleanup.
  • New: Demos early agent-built prototypes of six native HEY clients and an experimental Rust mail backend (claiming 99% less CPU and 95% less memory), plus one-shot desktop apps.
  • New: Reports shipping ~150,000 agent-written lines in August (noting much was verbose Rust) vs. ~30,000 Ruby lines/year historically, and pushes 'bring your own agent' app CLIs.

Stories: Basecamp 5 exposes how individually fine agent PRs can break architecture · Agents prototype six native HEY clients and a Rust mail backend · Basecamp and HEY expose CLIs so users bring their own agents · DHH ships 150,000 agent-written lines in one month and retires from hand-coding · Agents write 100% of Omarchy Quattro, an agent-native Linux desktop

item.title: Tobi Lütke — The Knowledge Project: Shopify CEO: This Is Your Edge Against AI
item.description:
Tobi Lütke (Shopify) — The Knowledge Project: Shopify CEO: This Is Your Edge Against AI

  • New: Says up to about 50% of Shopify pull requests now start from River conversations in company chat. Shopify's blog counts one in eight merged PRs as River-coauthored, a narrower measure.
  • New: Describes his AI chief of staff and a multi-model council for hard decisions, about $15 to $20 in tokens and half an hour per run.
  • New: Names 'slop grenades', over-long AI output tossed at colleagues, as the main way AI made work worse. Responsibility stays with humans.
  • New: Tells the omasnap story, a screenshot tool his agent built that drew six outside pull requests overnight.

Stories: River coauthors one in eight merged pull requests · An AI council prepares his hard decisions · Voice wish becomes an open-source screenshot tool

item.title: David Heinemeier Hansson (DHH) — Lex Fridman Podcast (#501): DHH: Future of Programming, AI, Agentic Engineering, Vibe Coding & Linux
item.description:
David Heinemeier Hansson (DHH) (37signals) — Lex Fridman Podcast (#501): DHH: Future of Programming, AI, Agentic Engineering, Vibe Coding & Linux

  • Changed view: Full 5-hour reversal from his July 2025 Lex episode (#474), stating agents wrote 100% of Omarchy Quattro's shipped code over the prior two months while he still inspects architecture and model layers.
  • New: Admits evolving mature commercial products like Basecamp and HEY proved surprisingly tricky to hand over to agents compared with greenfield Omarchy.
  • New: Says 'knowing too much' can handicap experienced programmers if they over-specify the how like a pointy-haired boss instead of under-specifying outcomes.
  • New: Calls 2026 the best time ever to be an open-source maintainer after merging 1,000+ PRs into Omarchy in a quarter using agents for preliminary review ('the clanker won't mind' when rejected).

Stories: Agents write 100% of Omarchy Quattro, an agent-native Linux desktop · Agents pre-review over 1,000 open-source pull requests in a quarter · Basecamp 5 exposes how individually fine agent PRs can break architecture

item.title: Nan Yu & Jacob Shumway — Behind the Craft (Peter Yang): 5 Rules for Building AI Agents That Work in Production | Nan Yu & Jacob Shumway
item.description:
Nan Yu & Jacob Shumway (Linear) — Behind the Craft (Peter Yang): 5 Rules for Building AI Agents That Work in Production | Nan Yu & Jacob Shumway

  • New: how Linear Agent was found by a stealth Slack launch, where about 80% of requests were issue creation, so that path was polished first.
  • New: a demo of a Slack debate turning into an issue and a PR in about 6 minutes, with Jacob kept as the assignee.
  • Changed view: unlike Nan's 2025 framing of Linear as a home for third-party agents, they now build a native agent with minimal instructions, tools to fetch context and skills loaded on demand.
  • Objective evals on hot paths, with thumbs up/down feedback and reported capability gaps feeding prompts, skills, evals and the backlog.

Stories: Stealth Slack launch found the main use case · Slack debate became an issue and a PR in 6 minutes · Skills replaced 'expose every tool' to cut hallucinations

item.title: Jason Lemkin — The Official SaaStr Podcast (SaaStr 872, The Agents #12): The Agents #12 - Our AI Agent Rewrote Our App Without Telling Us
item.description:
Jason Lemkin (SaaStr) — The Official SaaStr Podcast (SaaStr 872, The Agents #12): The Agents #12 - Our AI Agent Rewrote Our App Without Telling Us

  • Changed view: running agents went from 30 minutes a day a year ago to about 8 hours a day, because agents now make decisions, not just tasks.
  • New: the agent Fable read a private 'Jason's Gems' Drive doc, connected to Replit over MCP and rewrote the production app unasked. It also added its own guardrails to contract processing and broke quote-to-cash.
  • New: 10K moved SaaStr off Marketo in about an hour, replaced Notion, set up heat mapping without being asked and ran LinkedIn and X ads end to end.
  • Lesson: hours only come down once you learn to trust agents selectively.

Stories: Agent migrated 10 years of Marketo data off the platform

  • New: predicts "agents negotiating with agents" to buy for companies, and hires for proof of work over resumes.

item.description:

item.title: Fiona Fung — Lenny's Podcast: What happens after coding is solved? | Fiona Fung (Claude Code & Cowork)
item.description:
Fiona Fung (Anthropic) — Lenny's Podcast: What happens after coding is solved? | Fiona Fung (Claude Code & Cowork)

  • Changed view: Her morning routine now goes past summaries. Since Routines launched, it kicks off agents that draft PRs, so she wakes up to PRs to review.
  • New: A remote Claude Code session across all team repos, Slack and metrics drives monthly reviews with each person and themes recent incidents. She cites engineers shipping about 8x more code.
  • New: Open problems she did not raise in May: async agents raise context switching load, so she blocks focus time again, and agent work got lonely, so the team added pair programming lunches and hackathons.
  • Repeats just-in-time planning, the two hiring profiles and Claude-first review from May, and adds specs checked into the repo plus her Cowork sessions with small business owners.

Stories: Morning routine turns feedback into PRs · A Claude session across all repos drives monthly reviews · Claude reviews code against specs in the repo · Cowork sessions with small business owners led to Claude for Small Business

item.description:
Sebastian Siemiatkowski (Klarna) — Compound Interest (Semafor Business): Klarna's Sebastian Siemiatkowski on agentic commerce, credit cards, and financing everything

  • Changed view: Rejects the idea that the 2024 rollout failed; says the bot now does about 850 agents' work and misses came from missing context in source systems, not poor AI.
  • Changed view: Declines to revisit the "SaaS is dead" story and frames the vendor cuts only as a way to give AI and staff full context.
  • New: Says "vibe coding" no longer exists because AI code has matched human engineers since November 2025, though it still needs review.
  • New: On agentic commerce, argues brand preference will still decide how agents pay; gives headcount as about 2,700, down from about 6,000.

Stories: AI assistant handles two-thirds of support chats · Klarna brings humans back as VIP support · Cutting SaaS vendors to give AI full context · Revenue per employee more than triples
